capitals.note: Fretilin 'declared victory in the capital city of Dili' and declared independence on 28 November 1975 (occupation page); Indonesian forces invaded on 7 December 1975 and the state holds no land from July 1976 to October 1999, so no capital is drawn in those years (split by the se-04-c reviewer).

capitals.name: Dili
capitals.note: Infobox capital Dili; INTERFET 'entered Dili on 20 September' 1999 (occupation page) and the UN took over the administration on 25 October 1999.

correction.text: Portuguese Timor as the territory Fretilin declared independent on 28 November 1975, before the Indonesian invasion of 7 December; the grid outline is the one Cliopatria draws from 2006, including the Oecusse exclave

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no row before 2006. Fretilin 'unilaterally declared independence' on 28 November 1975 (East Timor page), nine days before the invasion. The Indonesian occupation page says Batugade, on the western border, was captured on 8 October 1975 and Balibo and Maliana eight days later, so the declared state did not hold all of its land; the contest events carry that. The state is then absent from 1976 to 1998 (Indonesia's republic-of-indonesia_1976 shape includes East Timor).

correction.text: the same outline as the 2006 shape, held from the Indonesian withdrawal of October 1999 (UN administration, UNTAET) and independent from 20 May 2002; the shape is unchanged and only the start year moves

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's East Timor row begins in 2006, but 'by 31 October 1999 the last Indonesian troops had left East Timor' (occupation page), UNTAET took over on 25 October 1999 (East Timor page) and independence came on 20 May 2002. republic-of-indonesia dossier already ends Indonesian rule here (its keyframe 1999-2005).

18,567 km2 against the infobox's 15,007 km2 (lead; the geography section gives 14,874): ratio 1.24, inside the factor of two. On the grid the shape has 5 cells outside {country: East Timor} and misses 2 of its 54, a generous outline, not a different land; it includes the Oecusse exclave, whose 1914 Permanent Court of Arbitration boundary 'remains the international boundary' with Indonesia. The pages mention no border change after 1999, so the shape stands to 2023.
Identical to the 2006 outline; nothing on the page moves the land.

region.text: 'declared an independent East Timor on 28 November 1975'

ledger.note: 1975: Fretilin declares East Timor independent at Dili (28 November). 'Fretilin declared victory in the capital city of Dili and declared an independent East Timor on 28 November 1975'; the East Timor page: Fretilin 'unilaterally declared independence'. Portuguese Timor is the land; the Indonesian forces already held Batugade (8 October).

region.text: East Timor, invaded on 7 December 1975 in Operasi Seroja

ledger.note: 7 December 1975: Indonesia invades. 'On 7 December 1975, Indonesian forces invaded East Timor'; Operasi Seroja was 'the largest military operation ever carried out by that nation'. Portugal cut diplomatic ties the next day; the UN General Assembly called on Indonesia to 'withdraw without delay'. Fretilin 'protected at least 40% of the population' in the interior in 1975-1977 (not drawn).

region.text: East Timor, annexed as Indonesia's 27th province

ledger.note: 17 July 1976: Indonesia annexes East Timor. 'On 17 July 1976, Indonesia formally annexed East Timor as its 27th province.' Resistance goes on: the 'encirclement and annihilation' campaign began in September 1977 and Nicolau Lobato was killed on 31 December 1978, but the land is drawn as Indonesia's from this date.

region.text: East Timor, annexed as Indonesia's 27th province

ledger.note: 1976: East Timor passes to Indonesia (17 July). The infobox gives a de jure Indonesian occupation of '7 December 1975 - 20 May 2002' and a de facto one to 31 October 1999; the East Timor page dates Indonesia's declaration of East Timor as its 27th province to the same day. The state is absent from the map until October 1999.

region.text: East Timor after the 30 August 1999 referendum: INTERFET 'entered Dili on 20 September and by 31 October the last Indonesian troops had left'

ledger.note: October 1999: Indonesia leaves East Timor and the UN takes over. 'INTERFET entered Dili on 20 September and by 31 October the last Indonesian troops had left East Timor'; UNTAET 'was established at the end of October' (occupation page), on 25 October 1999 (East Timor page), and administered the land for two years. The map gives the land back to East Timor under UN administration.

20 May 2002: East Timor becomes independent as the Democratic Republic of Timor-Leste, when the Constitution came into force and the UN recognised the independence; it joined the UN on 27 September 2002. Same state and colour (rule 2).

zones.text: East Timor, invaded on 7 December 1975 and annexed on 17 July 1976

wars.outcome: Indonesia invaded on 7 December 1975, annexed East Timor on 17 July 1976 and withdrew by 31 October 1999 after the UN-supervised referendum of 30 August 1999; the UN administered the land until independence on 20 May 2002.
wars.note: Infobox 7 December 1975 - 31 October 1999 (de jure to 20 May 2002); result '1999 East Timorese crisis'. The republic-of-indonesia dossier carries the same contest (December 1975 to July 1976), the gain and the loss with this state as counterpart.

certainty.note: The land border with Indonesia is the 1914 Permanent Court of Arbitration line, which 'remains the international boundary' (about 125 km); the Oecusse exclave sits inside Indonesian territory. The 2018 Timor Gap settlement is a maritime boundary and is not drawn. In 1975 the declared state did not hold the border towns (Batugade fell on 8 October 1975).

notes: Written for batch se-04-c with two pages (East Timor, Indonesian occupation of East Timor); the budget was 1-2. DESIGN CHOICE: Cliopatria's row starts in 2006, but the republic-of-indonesia dossier (se-04-a) already records a contest with 'east-timor' from December 1975, a gain in July 1976 and a loss in October 1999, each with this slug as counterpart; the se-04-a notes also ask for an earlier east-timor start. So this dossier starts on 28 November 1975, when Fretilin declared independence (the East Timor page dates the independence declaration to that day and calls it unilateral), has no land from July 1976 to September 1999 (as kingdom-of-cambodia has none in 1975-1993) and holds the land again from the Indonesian withdrawal, UN-administered until 20 May 2002. A reviewer who prefers a start at the internationally recognised independence (20 May 2002) must move the found event to 2002 and the republic-of-indonesia counterparts to a UNTAET dossier. Cliopatria: the 2006 shape is kept (ratio 1.24 to the infobox area, generous by 5 grid cells); two new keyframes (1975 and 1999-2005) cover what the row lacks. No border change after 1999 appears on either page. Page silent: the infobox of the East Timor page was garbled; the page gives no date for the referendum day (30 August 1999 is on the occupation page), no end date for UNTAET (independence 20 May 2002 is its end in practice), no 2005 or 2012-13 land-boundary agreements with Indonesia, nothing on the Noelbesi/Oben/Bijael Sunan areas; it dates Law 3/2014 (18 June 2014, effective January 2015) making Oecusse a Special Administrative Region, which is not a territorial event. Fretilin's interior zones of 1975-1978 and the Falintil resistance to 1999 are not drawn (no extent on the pages; the occupation page says Fretilin 'protected at least 40% of the population' in 1975-1977). UNTAET is not given its own dossier: the 1999 gain names republic-of-indonesia as the counterpart and UNTAET appears only in notes. No rulers are given (no list opened).
